name: INSACERMO_CPMP2015_BLIND_PLANNER_PREREG_V1
purpose: Third-domain pre-specified real-data structural replication of the INSACERMO sequential planner.

scenario_selection.rule: From coseal/aslib_data, choose the first alphabetically listed scenario not already used in the INSACERMO real-data sequence that has runtime performance, at least three algorithms, and at least ten deterministic features in description.txt. ASP-POTASSCO and BNSL-2016 were already used; CPMP-2015 is the next eligible scenario.

actions.selection_rule: Use the first two algorithms in description.txt metadata order as the base set and the third as the single REPAIR candidate. The fourth is reserved and not used in the primary test. This rule was fixed before reading algorithm_runs.arff.

good_action.definition: An algorithm is Good for an instance iff runstatus is ok and runtime is strictly below the official 3600-second cutoff.
good_action.objective: safe solvability, not runtime optimization among successful algorithms

cohort.definition: Fixed base-actionable cohort: all instances for which at least one of the two base algorithms is Good.
cohort.reason: Keeps the primary question conditional on worlds actionable under the original capability set and prevents impossible-to-base-solve worlds from being silently converted into an information problem.

probe_library.selection_rule: First 10 deterministic features listed in description.txt, fixed before reading outcomes.
probe_library.coarsening: For each numeric feature, quartile bins computed on the fixed cohort using feature values only. Duplicate quantile cuts are collapsed. Missing values, if present, form an explicit MISSING category. No outcome labels or algorithm runtimes are used to choose cuts.

safe_representation: For every realized observation cell induced by the selected probes, there exists at least one common Good action in the current capability set for every instance in that cell.

planner.search: Exhaustive over all 2^10 probe subsets under base and repaired capability sets.
planner.optimal_frontier: All safe states of globally minimum total structural cost. First-move route kinds are inferred from minimum-cost plans; ties are retained rather than forced to one label.

primary_endpoints: minimum probe count required for safety under base capabilities
minimum probe count required after the frozen REPAIR
whether capability expansion strictly reduces the minimum information requirement
whether a mixed PROBE+REPAIR route is necessary (start unsafe, PROBE-only unsafe, REPAIR-only unsafe, combined safe)
secondary_endpoints: partition entropy in bits at minimum-probe safe states
size of the optimal terminal frontier
PRESERVE stress: whether deleting one probe from an optimal terminal destroys safety

frozen_interpretation_rules.positive_capability_information_replicat: Minimum probes after REPAIR is strictly smaller than minimum probes under base capabilities. If base is unsolvable with all 10 frozen probes but repaired is solvable with a finite subset, count as a strong positive structural replication.
frozen_interpretation_rules.mixed_route_replication: No-probe base is unsafe, no-probe repaired is unsafe, and at least one repaired state with one or more frozen probes is safe while no probe-only state is safe.
frozen_interpretation_rules.null: REPAIR does not reduce the minimum probe requirement and does not create a previously unreachable safe representation.
frozen_interpretation_rules.negative: REPAIR increases minimum structural cost or destroys safety; report without changing protocol.

preserve_rule: A forgetting step deleting a probe from a safe terminal is legal only if the resulting coarser representation remains safe under the declared future capability state. Unsafe deletions are counted as PRESERVE-rejected.
analysis_boundary: Deterministic finite empirical planner test. No causal, population, stochastic, continuous-state, or infinite-horizon claim. The protocol is frozen before CPMP-2015/algorithm_runs.arff is opened.
